entries.description: Raw librdkafka properties merged after the security block, for options the typed fields do not model.
entries.full_description: Raw librdkafka properties merged after the security block, for options the typed fields do not model. Reserved keys (bootstrap.servers, group.id, enable.auto.commit, partition.assignment.strategy) are rejected at config load.

entries.description: Maximum messages returned per poll batch.
entries.full_description: Maximum messages returned per poll batch. Higher improves throughput; lower reduces latency.

entries.description: Maximum time (ms) between poll calls before Kafka considers the consumer dead and triggers a rebalance.
entries.full_description: Maximum time (ms) between poll calls before Kafka considers the consumer dead and triggers a rebalance. Increase for long-running tasks.

entries.description: Session timeout (ms) for group membership.
entries.full_description: Session timeout (ms) for group membership. Without a heartbeat within this window the broker removes the consumer from the group.

entries.description: Interval (ms) between heartbeats to the broker.
entries.full_description: Interval (ms) between heartbeats to the broker. Keep below session_timeout_ms / 3.

entries.description: What to do with a message whose value fails input_model parsing.
entries.full_description: What to do with a message whose value fails input_model parsing. 'skip' passes it to arrange() with payload=None and msg.parse_error set; 'dlq' excludes it from arrange(), writes a ParseFailurePayload to the DLQ topic, and commits once the write is confirmed; 'raise' fails fast — a MessageParseError stops the partition processor.

entries.description: Base URL of a Kafka-UI instance for deep links.
entries.full_description: Base URL of a Kafka-UI instance for deep links. Together with ui_cluster_name, renders an icon next to every partition:offset that opens Kafka-UI filtered on that message; empty disables the links.

entries.description: Cluster name as configured in Kafka-UI, used in the deep links.
entries.full_description: Cluster name as configured in Kafka-UI, used in the deep links. Both this and ui_url must be set for the links to appear.

entries.description: Delay the first Kafka subscribe until a shared wall-clock boundary, so a rolling-deploy fleet converges on one rebalance instead of N.
entries.full_description: Delay the first Kafka subscribe until a shared wall-clock boundary, so a rolling-deploy fleet converges on one rebalance instead of N. Disable for snappy single-worker dev runs.

entries.description: Minimum seconds to sleep before aligning — a buffer for slow init (DB connects, cache warm-up).
entries.full_description: Minimum seconds to sleep before aligning — a buffer for slow init (DB connects, cache warm-up).

entries.description: Alignment interval in seconds.
entries.full_description: Alignment interval in seconds. Workers wake at the next Unix-epoch multiple — the default 10 aligns on :00/:10/:20/:30/:40/:50 of every minute.

entries.description: Default binary path for all tasks.
entries.full_description: Default binary path for all tasks. None means each ExecutorTask returned by arrange() must carry its own binary_path, otherwise the task fails with a clear error.

entries.description: Environment variables passed to all executor subprocesses.
entries.full_description: Environment variables passed to all executor subprocesses. Merged on top of the (filtered) parent process environment. Per-task env vars from ExecutorTask.env override these on conflict.

entries.description: When True, the parent process env is passed to subprocesses (with deny patterns applied — see env_inherit_deny).
entries.full_description: When True, the parent process env is passed to subprocesses (with deny patterns applied — see env_inherit_deny). Set False to run subprocesses with ONLY ExecutorConfig.env + ExecutorTask.env — fully isolated from parent env.

entries.description: Case-insensitive fnmatch patterns against parent env var names.
entries.full_description: Case-insensitive fnmatch patterns against parent env var names. Matching vars are NOT inherited by subprocesses, even when env_inherit_parent is True. Deliberately narrower than the recorder redaction list: a pattern here WITHHOLDS the variable from your binary, so names with common non-secret uses (AUTH_SERVICE_URL, CERT_PATH, PRIVATE_SUBNET) are excluded. Set to [] to fully trust the parent environment.

entries.description: Maximum concurrent subprocesses.
entries.full_description: Maximum concurrent subprocesses. Tasks beyond this limit wait in a queue.

entries.description: Wall-clock timeout (seconds) per subprocess.
entries.full_description: Wall-clock timeout (seconds) per subprocess. A process exceeding it is killed and treated as a failure.

entries.description: Maximum bytes of stdout retained per task.
entries.full_description: Maximum bytes of stdout retained per task. 0 (the default) = unlimited. When a process writes more, the retained prefix is cut at a UTF-8 character boundary, the rest is read and discarded (the process is never blocked on a full pipe), and ExecutorResult.stdout_truncated is set. Useful when subprocesses can emit very large output.

entries.description: Maximum bytes of stderr retained per task.
entries.full_description: Maximum bytes of stderr retained per task. 0 (the default) = unlimited. Same semantics as max_stdout_bytes, applied to the stderr stream; sets ExecutorResult.stderr_truncated on cut.

entries.description: Maximum messages collected per arrange() window.
entries.full_description: Maximum messages collected per arrange() window. Larger windows allow more batching in arrange(); smaller windows reduce latency.

entries.description: Maximum retry attempts per failed task (0 = no retries).
entries.full_description: Maximum retry attempts per failed task (0 = no retries). A task runs at most max_retries + 1 times.

entries.description: Maximum seconds to wait for in-flight executor tasks to finish during graceful shutdown or partition revocation.
entries.full_description: Maximum seconds to wait for in-flight executor tasks to finish during graceful shutdown or partition revocation. Set lower to speed up shutdown; set at least as high as task_timeout_seconds if you rely on clean final commits for every in-flight task. When drain times out, offsets for in-flight tasks are NOT committed (those messages will replay on restart — at-least-once).

entries.description: Pause threshold multiplier: Kafka consumption pauses when total queued messages reach max_executors * this value.
entries.full_description: Pause threshold multiplier: Kafka consumption pauses when total queued messages reach max_executors * this value.

entries.description: Resume threshold multiplier: Kafka consumption resumes when total queued messages drop to max(1, max_executors * this value).
entries.full_description: Resume threshold multiplier: Kafka consumption resumes when total queued messages drop to max(1, max_executors * this value).

entries.full_description: Target Kafka topic for output messages.

entries.full_description: Kafka brokers for this sink. Empty inherits kafka.brokers — and with it kafka.security and kafka.client_config (same cluster, same credentials). Setting brokers makes the sink self-contained with its own security block.

entries.full_description: Broker hostname verification. Unset uses librdkafka's default ("https", verification on). Set to "none" only for internal CAs that issue certificates without matching SANs — it disables a real protection.

entries.description: Raw librdkafka properties for this sink, merged after security.
entries.full_description: Raw librdkafka properties for this sink, merged after security. Only consulted when brokers is set.

entries.description: Bound on the producer flush that ends every delivery.
entries.full_description: Bound on the producer flush that ends every delivery. Without one, librdkafka flushes with no deadline and a wedged broker blocks the call until message.timeout.ms (300s by default) — and it blocks a producer executor thread while doing it, so a few stuck deliveries starve every other delivery on the same producer. On expiry the delivery fails with a transient error, which is what lets the circuit breaker see the outage. Kept deliberately generous: this is a last resort, not a latency target.

entries.description: PostgreSQL connection string (asyncpg-compatible), typically embedding user and password.
entries.full_description: PostgreSQL connection string (asyncpg-compatible), typically embedding user and password.

entries.full_description: Minimum connections in the asyncpg pool.

entries.full_description: Maximum connections in the asyncpg pool.

entries.description: Operator-authored SQL keyed by name.
entries.full_description: Operator-authored SQL keyed by name. A PostgresPayload with op='statement' and a matching `statement` name executes the entry with its `params` bound to the :name placeholders. This is the escape hatch for SQL the declarative payload fields cannot express — value-dependent expressions and guarded predicates. Keeping the SQL here rather than in the payload means message content can never reach the statement text.

entries.full_description: URL to a database management UI (e.g. pgAdmin), shown as a link in the operator UI.

entries.full_description: Which write operation to perform. Statements allow the update and delete ops only — an insert is fully expressible as a declarative payload and needs no template.

entries.full_description: Equality-or-richer predicate selecting the documents to write. Must be non-empty.

entries.full_description: Update document for the update ops, absent for the delete ops. A LIST is an aggregation pipeline — MongoDB's own mechanism for computed updates.

entries.full_description: Prefix prepended to all keys (e.g. 'cache:' produces keys like 'cache:my-key').

entries.description: Operator-authored Lua keyed by name.
entries.full_description: Operator-authored Lua keyed by name. A RedisPayload with op='script' and a matching `script` name runs the entry with its `keys` and `args` passed as KEYS and ARGV. This is the escape hatch for multi-step or conditional logic, and the only way to get server-side atomicity — a pipeline is not a transaction. Parameters are never interpolated into the body, so message content cannot alter what runs.

entries.description: URL to a Redis management UI (e.g. RedisInsight), shown as a link in the operator UI.
entries.full_description: URL to a Redis management UI (e.g. RedisInsight), shown as a link in the operator UI.

entries.full_description: Base directory for all writes. Payload paths resolve relative to it and must stay contained within it — absolute or traversing paths are rejected.

entries.description: URL to a file browser or related UI, shown as a link in the operator UI.
entries.full_description: URL to a file browser or related UI, shown as a link in the operator UI.

entries.description: Plugin-discovered sink instances.
entries.full_description: Plugin-discovered sink instances. Top-level keys are sink type names registered via [project.entry-points."drakkar.sinks"]; second-level keys are instance names; leaf dicts are plugin-defined config passed verbatim to the sink class constructor.

entries.description: Budget for one sink delivery, including the framework-internal transient retries.
entries.full_description: Budget for one sink delivery, including the framework-internal transient retries. A sink whose server stops answering while the TCP connection stays open would otherwise block its partition forever: the circuit breaker only sees a failure when a call returns. Sinks whose driver supports it also use this value for their own socket/command timeout, so the driver reports a specific error before this outer budget expires. Applies to close() during shutdown as well.

entries.description: Consecutive delivery failures before the circuit trips open.
entries.full_description: Consecutive delivery failures before the circuit trips open. 5 = trip on the 5th consecutive failure (4 prior failures did not trip, the 5th did). Intermittent failures with any success in between do not accumulate.

entries.description: Time the circuit stays fully open before the next delivery is allowed through as a half-open probe.
entries.full_description: Time the circuit stays fully open before the next delivery is allowed through as a half-open probe. While open, all deliveries route directly to DLQ — no attempt is made on the sink.

entries.description: DLQ Kafka topic name.
entries.full_description: DLQ Kafka topic name. Empty derives '{source_topic}_dlq' at runtime.

entries.description: Kafka brokers for the DLQ producer.
entries.full_description: Kafka brokers for the DLQ producer. Empty inherits kafka.brokers — and with it kafka.security and kafka.client_config, on the same same-cluster-means-same-credentials rule the Kafka sinks follow.

entries.description: Wire protocol.
entries.full_description: Wire protocol. PLAINTEXT (default) is unauthenticated and unencrypted. SSL adds TLS; SASL_PLAINTEXT adds authentication without encryption; SASL_SSL adds both and is what managed clusters normally require.

entries.description: SASL mechanism.
entries.full_description: SASL mechanism. Required when protocol is SASL_PLAINTEXT or SASL_SSL, and rejected otherwise so a mechanism that would be ignored is never left in the config. PLAIN and the SCRAM mechanisms additionally require sasl_username and sasl_password.

entries.full_description: SASL username (PLAIN / SCRAM mechanisms).

entries.full_description: SASL password. Prefer the DK_KAFKA__SECURITY__SASL_PASSWORD environment override over a literal in YAML; DK_* variables are withheld from executor subprocesses by the default executor.env_inherit_deny list.

entries.full_description: Broker hostname verification. Unset uses librdkafka's default ("https", verification on). Set to "none" only for internal CAs that issue certificates without matching SANs — it disables a real protection.

entries.description: Raw librdkafka properties for the DLQ producer, merged after security.
entries.full_description: Raw librdkafka properties for the DLQ producer, merged after security. Only consulted when brokers is set.

entries.description: Bound on the producer flush that ends every DLQ write.
entries.full_description: Bound on the producer flush that ends every DLQ write. Same rationale as KafkaSinkConfig.flush_timeout_seconds, and it matters more here: the DLQ is the last resort, so a DLQ write that blocks for message.timeout.ms stalls the partition it was meant to rescue. On expiry the write is reported as unconfirmed and the affected offsets stall.

entries.description: Strategy when the DLQ write itself fails.
entries.full_description: Strategy when the DLQ write itself fails. 'drop' logs CRITICAL, counts the loss, commits the offset, and keeps the pipeline moving; 'stall' leaves the offset uncommitted and pauses the partition until restart — no loss, at the cost of consumer lag.

entries.description: Serve Prometheus metrics over HTTP.
entries.full_description: Serve Prometheus metrics over HTTP.

entries.description: Port for the Prometheus metrics endpoint.
entries.full_description: Port for the Prometheus metrics endpoint.

entries.description: Task label keys whose numeric values are observed into the drakkar_task_label_value histogram at task completion, one time series per key (e.g. a file-size or line-count label).
entries.full_description: Task label keys whose numeric values are observed into the drakkar_task_label_value histogram at task completion, one time series per key (e.g. a file-size or line-count label). Values that do not parse as finite numbers are skipped.

entries.description: Task label key whose numeric value is the task cost — a number correlating with computational hardness (bytes, a computed score, any unit).
entries.full_description: Task label key whose numeric value is the task cost — a number correlating with computational hardness (bytes, a computed score, any unit). Empty (the default) disables the whole feature. Values that do not parse as finite numbers leave the task uncounted.

entries.description: Smallest cost worth counting.
entries.full_description: Smallest cost worth counting. Tasks below it carry no speed and enter no aggregate — useful when fixed overhead dominates small tasks and their speeds would mislead.

entries.description: Run the runtime health monitor: heartbeat lag tracking, stall stack sampling, and the data behind the debug UI's Runtime tab.
entries.full_description: Run the runtime health monitor: heartbeat lag tracking, stall stack sampling, and the data behind the debug UI's Runtime tab.

entries.description: Heartbeat interval.
entries.full_description: Heartbeat interval. Lag is measured as how late each tick fires; the sampler thread also checks heartbeat age at this interval. Smaller values narrow the attribution blind spot for short blocks at slightly more (still negligible) wakeups.

entries.description: Lag above this marks the runtime 'degraded'.
entries.full_description: Lag above this marks the runtime 'degraded'. Recovery to 'healthy' needs several consecutive clean ticks (hysteresis), so a flapping loop does not spam state transitions.

entries.description: Heartbeat age above this marks the runtime 'stalled' and starts stack sampling: the sampler thread captures what the runtime thread is executing until the heartbeat resumes.
entries.full_description: Heartbeat age above this marks the runtime 'stalled' and starts stack sampling: the sampler thread captures what the runtime thread is executing until the heartbeat resumes. Each stall becomes one runtime_stall recorder event with the stacks.

entries.description: Maximum distinct stack traces captured per stall.
entries.full_description: Maximum distinct stack traces captured per stall. Repeated samples of the same location collapse into one entry with a count; further distinct stacks past the cap are dropped.

entries.description: Interval between runtime_health sample events written to the flight recorder for cross-restart history.
entries.full_description: Interval between runtime_health sample events written to the flight recorder for cross-restart history. The fine-grained lag sparkline comes from an in-memory ring buffer instead and costs no database writes.

entries.description: Length of the in-memory lag history ring buffer (one max/avg aggregate per second) served to the debug UI sparkline.
entries.full_description: Length of the in-memory lag history ring buffer (one max/avg aggregate per second) served to the debug UI sparkline.

entries.description: Maximum length of one lag episode.
entries.full_description: Maximum length of one lag episode. An episode spans the time the runtime is degraded or stalled; on recovery (or at this cap, for incidents that outlive it) the monitor writes one runtime_lag_episode event with aggregated stacks and a verdict — blocked, cpu_bound, starved, or inconclusive.

entries.description: Opt-in flight-recorder profiler: when above 0, the sampler thread records a runtime_probe event with the runtime thread's stack every interval, regardless of health state.
entries.full_description: Opt-in flight-recorder profiler: when above 0, the sampler thread records a runtime_probe event with the runtime thread's stack every interval, regardless of health state. Useful for tuning production workloads and post-incident analysis; 0 (the default) disables it because it writes events for as long as the worker runs.

entries.description: Worker threads in asyncio's default to_thread executor.
entries.full_description: Worker threads in asyncio's default to_thread executor. 0 (the default) keeps Python's own sizing, min(32, cpu_count + 4). Set an explicit value when handler I/O concurrency is capped by the pool — e.g. many-core hosts doing wide blocking filesystem fan-out. Blocking I/O releases the GIL, so large values are legitimate here (unlike offload.max_threads); the trade-off is pressure on the storage behind the calls.

entries.description: Worker threads in the shared offload pool.
entries.full_description: Worker threads in the shared offload pool. 0 (the default) sizes the pool automatically from the executor pool: ceil(executor.max_executors / 4), with a minimum of 2 — e.g. pool 8 -> 2 threads, 9 -> 3, 13 -> 4. Calls beyond this many concurrent offloaded computations queue (FIFO) and show up in the drakkar_offload_queued gauge. More threads do not speed up pure-Python work (GIL); set an explicit value only when several partitions routinely offload at once and queueing delay matters, or when the offloaded code releases the GIL (numpy, compiled extensions).

entries.description: Log level: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, or CRITICAL.
entries.full_description: Log level: DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, or CRITICAL.

entries.description: Output format.
entries.full_description: Output format. 'json' produces machine-readable structured logs; 'console' produces colorized human-readable output for local development.

entries.description: Log output destination.
entries.full_description: Log output destination. "stderr" (default) or "stdout" for standard streams, or a file path for file output. File paths support template variables: {worker_id}, {cluster_name}. Example: "/var/log/drakkar/{worker_id}.log"

entries.description: Enable the whole UI feature: the server, flight-recorder persistence, and bundle serving.
entries.full_description: Enable the whole UI feature: the server, flight-recorder persistence, and bundle serving. Off skips all of it.

entries.description: Bind address for the UI server.
entries.full_description: Bind address for the UI server. Use 0.0.0.0 to expose on all interfaces.

entries.description: Port for the UI server.
entries.full_description: Port for the UI server.

entries.description: Bearer token for the UI. **Empty (the default) disables auth** entirely — every endpoint (including database download, merge, and message-probe) is reachable without credentials and the WebSocket live-event stream skips both token and Origin checks.
entries.full_description: Bearer token for the UI. **Empty (the default) disables auth** entirely — every endpoint (including database download, merge, and message-probe) is reachable without credentials and the WebSocket live-event stream skips both token and Origin checks. This is a deliberate opt-in design: no endpoint stops a worker, replays Kafka messages, mutates sinks, or commits offsets, and Drakkar is intended for deployment inside a private contour (VPC / internal cluster / operator-only ingress). Most endpoints are read-only, but the probe and merge routes are not — close those with ``probe_enabled`` / ``merge_enabled``, which act independently of this token. A startup warning fires whenever the UI is enabled without a token so the unauthenticated posture is visible in logs, naming whichever side-effecting endpoint is still enabled. When set to a non-empty value, protected HTTP endpoints require an ``Authorization: Bearer <token>`` header or ``?token=<token>`` query parameter; WebSocket connections without a valid token are closed with code 4401, and the Origin header is validated against ``allowed_ws_origins`` (or the request Host header if that list is empty). Comparison uses ``secrets.compare_digest`` to avoid timing side-channels. Trailing/leading whitespace is stripped on load to avoid silent mismatches when YAML accidentally quotes spaces.

entries.description: Explicit allowlist of WebSocket origins.
entries.full_description: Explicit allowlist of WebSocket origins. Empty list with non-empty auth_token defaults to same-origin only; empty list with empty auth_token = no origin check (dev workflow preserved).

entries.description: Serve ``POST /api/v1/debug/probe``.
entries.full_description: Serve ``POST /api/v1/debug/probe``. This is the one UI endpoint that runs caller-supplied bytes through the live handler and the real executor subprocess pool, so it is neither read-only nor free: it competes with production traffic for executor slots. Set to false to serve 403 instead — independently of ``auth_token``, so a deployment that cannot set a token can still close the endpoint, and a deployment that has one can still close it as defence in depth. Probes never write sinks, recorder rows, cache entries, or offsets, so switching it off costs no pipeline behaviour.

entries.description: Serve ``POST /api/v1/debug/merge``.
entries.full_description: Serve ``POST /api/v1/debug/merge``. This is the one UI endpoint that writes to disk: each call creates a new ``merged-<ts>.db`` in ``ui.recorder.db_dir`` and nothing reclaims it, so repeated calls grow unbounded. Set to false to serve 403 instead — independently of ``auth_token``, per the reasoning on ``probe_enabled``.

entries.description: Serve ``GET /api/v1/debug/kafka/*`` — ad-hoc reads of the configured topics (source, dlq, and each Kafka sink by instance name; never an arbitrary topic).
entries.full_description: Serve ``GET /api/v1/debug/kafka/*`` — ad-hoc reads of the configured topics (source, dlq, and each Kafka sink by instance name; never an arbitrary topic). Reads use assign()-only consumers that join no consumer group and commit no offsets, so they are invisible to the pipeline. Set to false to serve 403 instead — independently of ``auth_token``, per the reasoning on ``probe_enabled``. When the resolved Kafka security of any readable topic is not PLAINTEXT while ``auth_token`` is empty, startup logs a warning naming the exposed aliases (the API stays available — gate it with ``auth_token`` or close it here).

entries.description: Externally reachable URL of this worker's UI, used for cross-worker links in the workers list.
entries.full_description: Externally reachable URL of this worker's UI, used for cross-worker links in the workers list. Empty derives http://<ip>:<port> from the bind address.

entries.description: A discovered worker whose newest heartbeat is older than this many seconds is reported offline in the workers list.
entries.full_description: A discovered worker whose newest heartbeat is older than this many seconds is reported offline in the workers list. Size it to at least 2-3x the largest ``ui.recorder.state_sync_interval_seconds`` in the fleet so a healthy worker never flaps offline between heartbeats.

entries.description: Environment variable names captured into the worker_config snapshot — for recording deployment metadata like GIT_SHA or K8S_POD_NAME.
entries.full_description: Environment variable names captured into the worker_config snapshot — for recording deployment metadata like GIT_SHA or K8S_POD_NAME.

entries.description: Maximum rows returned to the web UI in list views.
entries.full_description: Maximum rows returned to the web UI in list views.

entries.description: Minimum task duration (ms) to emit a slow_task_completed / slow_task_failed log line.
entries.full_description: Minimum task duration (ms) to emit a slow_task_completed / slow_task_failed log line. 0 logs all tasks.

entries.description: Minimum task duration (ms) to broadcast to the live UI over WebSocket.
entries.full_description: Minimum task duration (ms) to broadcast to the live UI over WebSocket. Failed tasks always appear. 0 shows all tasks.

entries.description: Base URL of the Prometheus server used for UI links.
entries.full_description: Base URL of the Prometheus server used for UI links. Empty shows no Prometheus links.

entries.description: Rate interval used in PromQL rate() expressions in UI links (e.g. '1m', '5m', '15m').
entries.full_description: Rate interval used in PromQL rate() expressions in UI links (e.g. '1m', '5m', '15m').

entries.description: PromQL label filter for worker-scoped queries, with {worker_id}, {cluster_name}, {metrics_port}, and {debug_port} template variables.
entries.full_description: PromQL label filter for worker-scoped queries, with {worker_id}, {cluster_name}, {metrics_port}, and {debug_port} template variables. Empty defaults to instance="{hostname}:{metrics_port}".

entries.description: PromQL label filter for cluster-wide queries, same template variables as prometheus_worker_label.
entries.full_description: PromQL label filter for cluster-wide queries, same template variables as prometheus_worker_label. Empty hides cluster-wide links.

entries.description: Custom links shown in the dashboard navigation.
entries.full_description: Custom links shown in the dashboard navigation. Each entry is a dict with name and url keys; url supports the {worker_id}, {cluster_name}, {metrics_port}, and {debug_port} template variables.

entries.description: Named URL bases for probe-details link templates, e.g. ``{jira: 'https://jira.internal.example.com'}``.
entries.full_description: Named URL bases for probe-details link templates, e.g. ``{jira: 'https://jira.internal.example.com'}``. A template such as ``{jira}/browse/{value}`` resolves ``{jira}`` from this map, so code declares the link shape once and each environment supplies its own hosts. A base referenced by a registered layout but missing here logs one startup warning and the UI renders plain text for it.

entries.description: Path to a deployment-provided JS module of custom cell renderers, served as-is at ``GET /api/v1/ui/renderers.js``.
entries.full_description: Path to a deployment-provided JS module of custom cell renderers, served as-is at ``GET /api/v1/ui/renderers.js``. Empty (the default) disables the feature — the route then 404s and identity reports ``custom_renderers: false``. When set, the file must exist at startup or the worker fails to boot; its content is trusted the same as any other backend config (it runs same-origin in the operator UI).

entries.description: Serve the consume-pause API (``/api/v1/debug/consume-pause``) and show the pause control on the Live page.
entries.full_description: Serve the consume-pause API (``/api/v1/debug/consume-pause``) and show the pause control on the Live page. Off by default: pausing stops message intake for the chosen duration, which is a production-affecting act — enable it deliberately, for debug-friendly deployments.

entries.description: Preset pause durations (seconds) offered as one-click buttons on the Live page.
entries.full_description: Preset pause durations (seconds) offered as one-click buttons on the Live page. The API itself accepts any duration between 1 and 3600 seconds regardless of the presets.

entries.description: Directory for the recorder SQLite files.
entries.full_description: Directory for the recorder SQLite files. Empty runs memory-only: no files, no history — the live WebSocket view keeps working. Use a shared filesystem for cross-worker autodiscovery and merge.

entries.description: Write processing events to the events table.
entries.full_description: Write processing events to the events table. Off, the live WebSocket view still streams, but History, Trace, and task queries return nothing.

entries.description: Write the worker config snapshot to the worker_config table — what makes the worker discoverable by peers sharing the same db_dir.
entries.full_description: Write the worker config snapshot to the worker_config table — what makes the worker discoverable by peers sharing the same db_dir.

entries.description: Periodically snapshot worker counters (uptime, partitions, pool utilization, queue depth) to the worker_state table.
entries.full_description: Periodically snapshot worker counters (uptime, partitions, pool utilization, queue depth) to the worker_state table.

entries.description: Seconds between worker_state snapshots — also the heartbeat cadence worker liveness is judged by.
entries.full_description: Seconds between worker_state snapshots — also the heartbeat cadence worker liveness is judged by.

entries.description: How often to roll over to a new SQLite file.
entries.full_description: How often to roll over to a new SQLite file.

entries.description: Archive rotated-out DB files instead of deleting them outright.
entries.full_description: Archive rotated-out DB files instead of deleting them outright.

entries.description: How much recent history the archive pass keeps queryable; must be >= rotation_interval_hours.
entries.full_description: How much recent history the archive pass keeps queryable; must be >= rotation_interval_hours.

entries.description: How long archived files are kept before deletion.
entries.full_description: How long archived files are kept before deletion. Defaults to 30 days so a worker cannot fill its disk unattended. 0 = keep archives forever (a startup warning names the choice); any other value must cover at least two archive windows (archive_retention_days * 24 >= 2 * archive_window_hours).

entries.description: How often the background warmer sweeps db_dir, computing statistics for database files the .dbstats cache does not know yet and purging entries for deleted files.
entries.full_description: How often the background warmer sweeps db_dir, computing statistics for database files the .dbstats cache does not know yet and purging entries for deleted files. Cheap when everything is already cached — one directory listing plus one small SELECT.

entries.description: How many cold (uncached) database files one /api/v1/debug/databases request may fully scan inline.
entries.full_description: How many cold (uncached) database files one /api/v1/debug/databases request may fully scan inline. Files beyond the cap return immediately with stats_pending=true and fill in as the warmer catches up. 0 = requests never scan; matters only on a cold cache (first boot over a pre-existing directory).

entries.description: Store subprocess stdout/stderr content in task events.
entries.full_description: Store subprocess stdout/stderr content in task events. Off drops output content from all of them.

entries.description: Store each task's stdin content (capped at stdin_max_bytes) in the task_started event metadata, so the debug UI can show exactly what a task consumed.
entries.full_description: Store each task's stdin content (capped at stdin_max_bytes) in the task_started event metadata, so the debug UI can show exactly what a task consumed. Off by default: on a high-fan-out workload stdin is the largest payload the recorder would write. Failed tasks always store their stdin (capped) on the task_failed event, regardless of this flag.

entries.description: Byte cap for stored stdin content (store_stdin, and the always-on failed-task capture).
entries.full_description: Byte cap for stored stdin content (store_stdin, and the always-on failed-task capture). 0 = unlimited. Truncation is flagged as stdin_truncated in the event metadata.

entries.description: Seconds between recorder buffer flushes to SQLite.
entries.full_description: Seconds between recorder buffer flushes to SQLite.

entries.description: In-memory event buffer capacity.
entries.full_description: In-memory event buffer capacity. When full, the oldest events are evicted and counted in drakkar_recorder_dropped_events_total.

entries.description: Consecutive failed flush attempts tolerated per batch before it is dropped (counted in drakkar_recorder_flush_batches_dropped_total).
entries.full_description: Consecutive failed flush attempts tolerated per batch before it is dropped (counted in drakkar_recorder_flush_batches_dropped_total).

entries.description: Minimum task duration (ms) to persist a task event at all.
entries.full_description: Minimum task duration (ms) to persist a task event at all. 0 persists everything.

entries.description: Minimum task duration (ms) to include args/stdout/stderr in the persisted event.
entries.full_description: Minimum task duration (ms) to include args/stdout/stderr in the persisted event. Faster tasks keep their row without output data.

entries.description: Accept handler annotations (self.annotate(...)) and write them to the events table.
entries.full_description: Accept handler annotations (self.annotate(...)) and write them to the events table.

entries.description: Byte cap for one annotation payload; larger payloads are dropped whole.
entries.full_description: Byte cap for one annotation payload; larger payloads are dropped whole. 0 disables the cap.

entries.description: Total annotation bytes one hook invocation may write; further payloads past it are dropped.
entries.full_description: Total annotation bytes one hook invocation may write; further payloads past it are dropped. 0 disables the cap.

entries.description: Cap on the payload copy included in the warning log when an annotation is dropped.
entries.full_description: Cap on the payload copy included in the warning log when an annotation is dropped. 0 disables the cap.

entries.description: Resolve and serve the drakkar-ui bundle.
entries.full_description: Resolve and serve the drakkar-ui bundle. Off means no UI at all (no fetch, no cache read): the JSON API, the health probes and the event WebSocket keep working, and page requests answer 503.

entries.description: The "owner/name" GitHub repo that publishes UI bundles.
entries.full_description: The "owner/name" GitHub repo that publishes UI bundles. Empty disables fetching — only an already-cached bundle is served, which is how an air-gapped deployment pins itself to a bundle staged with the drakkar-ui CLI.

entries.description: Known-good UI release tag this backend is built against (e.g. "v1.2.0"); the contract is API-major compatible.
entries.full_description: Known-good UI release tag this backend is built against (e.g. "v1.2.0"); the contract is API-major compatible. Empty means "no pinned version".

entries.description: Bundle cache root override.
entries.full_description: Bundle cache root override. Empty uses the per-user cache dir ($XDG_CACHE_HOME/drakkar/ui, falling back to ~/.cache/drakkar/ui — the conventional per-user cache location, so co-located workers share one cache).

entries.description: Resolve the latest release tag on startup instead of only the pinned version (the "check for a new version" toggle).
entries.full_description: Resolve the latest release tag on startup instead of only the pinned version (the "check for a new version" toggle). Already-cached versions are never re-downloaded — release tags are immutable.

entries.description: Maximum probe.set/append/update calls recorded per probe run.
entries.full_description: Maximum probe.set/append/update calls recorded per probe run. The first write past the cap records one ProbeError; further writes are dropped silently.

entries.description: Maximum total serialized size (bytes) of all probe-details writes per probe run.
entries.full_description: Maximum total serialized size (bytes) of all probe-details writes per probe run. Past it, writes are dropped like the max_writes cap.

entries.description: Timeline keeps the newest history_factor x executor.max_executors tasks.
entries.full_description: Timeline keeps the newest history_factor x executor.max_executors tasks.

entries.description: Oldest task age the timeline shows, in minutes.
entries.full_description: Oldest task age the timeline shows, in minutes.

entries.description: First-match-wins rules coloring timeline task bars from labels and task fields.
entries.full_description: First-match-wins rules coloring timeline task bars from labels and task fields.

entries.description: Label whose value draws as a short chip at the task bar's right edge (truncated to 16 chars).
entries.full_description: Label whose value draws as a short chip at the task bar's right edge (truncated to 16 chars).

entries.description: Label whose value draws at the task bar's left edge, in the space the tag leaves over (truncated to 32 chars).
entries.full_description: Label whose value draws at the task bar's left edge, in the space the tag leaves over (truncated to 32 chars).

entries.description: Numeric label bound to the toolbar threshold input: tasks at or above the typed value are emphasized, the rest dimmed.
entries.full_description: Numeric label bound to the toolbar threshold input: tasks at or above the typed value are emphasized, the rest dimmed.

entries.description: String label bound to the toolbar text input: tasks whose value contains the typed text are emphasized, the rest dimmed.
entries.full_description: String label bound to the toolbar text input: tasks whose value contains the typed text are emphasized, the rest dimmed.

entries.description: Label that draws one vertical pin above the strip per distinct value — e.g. a batch or request id.
entries.full_description: Label that draws one vertical pin above the strip per distinct value — e.g. a batch or request id.

entries.description: Declared custom timeline event types drawn as markers, ranges, or flag pins on the live timeline.
entries.full_description: Declared custom timeline event types drawn as markers, ranges, or flag pins on the live timeline.

entries.description: Directory of a prebuilt static docs site served at /docs/.
entries.full_description: Directory of a prebuilt static docs site served at /docs/. Empty disables the feature.

entries.description: Nav-entry label and default drawer heading in the UI.
entries.full_description: Nav-entry label and default drawer heading in the UI.

entries.description: Contextual anchors opening the named docs page from matching UI surfaces.
entries.full_description: Contextual anchors opening the named docs page from matching UI surfaces.

entries.description: Give every handler a self.cache key/value store, memory-backed with write-behind SQLite.
entries.full_description: Give every handler a self.cache key/value store, memory-backed with write-behind SQLite. Off, the handler cache API is absent.

entries.description: Directory for the cache SQLite file.
entries.full_description: Directory for the cache SQLite file. Empty falls back to ui.recorder.db_dir; with neither set, the cache warns at startup and disables itself.

entries.description: Seconds between write-behind flushes of dirty entries to SQLite.
entries.full_description: Seconds between write-behind flushes of dirty entries to SQLite.

entries.description: Seconds between cleanup passes deleting expired rows and refreshing DB-size gauges.
entries.full_description: Seconds between cleanup passes deleting expired rows and refreshing DB-size gauges.

entries.description: Cap for in-memory LRU entries.
entries.full_description: Cap for in-memory LRU entries. Default 10_000 prevents unbounded growth under write-heavy workloads. Set to None for explicitly unbounded cache.

entries.description: Pull cache entries from sibling workers' cache DBs on a periodic loop.
entries.full_description: Pull cache entries from sibling workers' cache DBs on a periodic loop. Off, flush and cleanup still run but nothing propagates across workers.

entries.description: Seconds between peer-sync cycles.
entries.full_description: Seconds between peer-sync cycles.

entries.description: Maximum rows pulled from one peer per sync cycle.
entries.full_description: Maximum rows pulled from one peer per sync cycle.

entries.description: Per-peer time budget (seconds) within one sync cycle.
entries.full_description: Per-peer time budget (seconds) within one sync cycle.

entries.description: Hard wall-clock cap on one peer-sync cycle.
entries.full_description: Hard wall-clock cap on one peer-sync cycle. When None, defaults to interval_seconds * 0.9. Prevents a single slow peer from starving the periodic task.

entries.description: Run the synchronous HTTP ingress.
entries.full_description: Run the synchronous HTTP ingress. Off, no server starts and the handler's HTTP hooks are never invoked.

entries.description: Interface the webapp binds.
entries.full_description: Interface the webapp binds. Use '127.0.0.1' to keep the endpoint host-local.

entries.description: Port the webapp binds.
entries.full_description: Port the webapp binds. Not shared with the operator UI or the metrics server.

entries.description: The single POST route the webapp registers.
entries.full_description: The single POST route the webapp registers. Must start with '/' and name a non-empty route.

entries.description: Call on_message_complete() after the executor fan-out and route returned payloads through the sinks.
entries.full_description: Call on_message_complete() after the executor fan-out and route returned payloads through the sinks. Off, sinks are skipped and the response carries sinks: null.

entries.description: Per-request budget in seconds.
entries.full_description: Per-request budget in seconds. On timeout the client receives a 504 with status='timeout' and remaining pipeline work is cooperatively cancelled.

entries.description: Cap on in-flight HTTP requests.
entries.full_description: Cap on in-flight HTTP requests. Requests beyond it receive an immediate 503 instead of queuing.

entries.description: Cap on a single POST body (bytes), counted from the stream so a lying Content-Length cannot bypass it.
entries.full_description: Cap on a single POST body (bytes), counted from the stream so a lying Content-Length cannot bypass it. Oversized requests receive 413 before parsing.

entries.description: List of webapp clients (tenants).
entries.full_description: List of webapp clients (tenants). Defaults to a single anonymous client with empty token and rpm=4 so the webapp works out of the box for development. Production deployments should configure named clients with non-empty tokens.
